definitions.explanation: Without anything or anyone in between.
Through direct personal experience or contact.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}に{直|じか}に{会|あ}って{話|はな}したい。
examples.english: I want to meet the president directly and talk.

examples.japanese: {現場|げんば}を{直|じか}に{見|み}てきた。
{床|ゆか}に{直|じか}に{座|すわ}る。
examples.english: To sit directly on the floor.

notes:
{直|じか}に is an adverb meaning directly or firsthand, emphasizing unmediated contact or experience.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {直|じか}に{会|あ}う (to meet directly/in person)
- {直|じか}に{見|み}る (to see firsthand)
- {直|じか}に{聞|き}く (to hear directly)
- {肌|はだ}に{直|じか}に{触|ふ}れる (to touch directly against the skin)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {直|じか}に vs. {直接|ちょくせつ}: Very similar in meaning. {直接|ちょくせつ} is slightly more formal and common; {直|じか}に has a more personal, physical nuance.
- {直|じか}に vs. じきに: Different words! じきに means "soon" or "shortly," not "directly."

Register: Neutral. Common in both spoken and written Japanese.
